chunks.text: Now let's talk about a very important technique which we call linear search
Let's take an example that you are sitting in your college canteen and you want samosas
So what you will do is you will search for samosas in the menu from top to bottom
Let's assume that our dosa is written at the top of the list
After that, our chole bhature are written
After that, our samosas are written
And after that, a sandwich is written, your fruit tea is written
Or some people like coke, so coke will be written
So there will be a list of this kind in which you will see first that this is not samosa, this is not samosa, this is not samosa, oh, I got it
And then you will go and buy the samosa
So in this way, when you scan things continuously, then we call this technique linear search
Now we have to find an element in the array, so we use this type of search technique
For example, we have an array, in the array there are elements 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16
Now we have to search for a key here, the key is 10
That is, we have to search for which index 10 comes in this array
So what we will do is first look at index 0, what is 10 here, then look at index 1, what is 10 here, so it is not here, it is not here
Then we will look at index 2, it is not here, we will look at index 3, it is not here, we will look at index 4, and here we will get 10
So we will return this index as our output, as our final answer
So in this type of technique, in which we are going up the index one by one and then we are seeing that here is our key, here is our key, here is our key
We call this technique linear search
And this is a very simple, very easy technique and now we will write its code
First of all, we have made an array, in the array all our marks are stored, in fact, instead of marks, we give it the name numbers
And here we have made our key, what is the key, 10, for 10 we have to search for which index this key is stored
So let's make a function, public static, let's keep its return type integer and give its name linear search
In linear search, we will pass an array named numbers and along with it we will pass our key
So in this whole number, we have to search for this key
And there is a case in which we are searching for such a key which is not there, so in that case we will return minus 1
For example, if we want to search for 54 for this array, then it does not exist in it, so in that case we will return minus 1
So what do we have to do for linear search, we have to run a loop
To run the loop, the loop will go from index 0 to the length of our array, that is, it will go to the length of numbers dot
And every time we will do i++
Now for every index, we will check if the number of i is equal to the number of the key, then in that case we will simply return our i
And if this does not happen, then in the last we will return minus 1, this return of minus 1 means that our key does not exist
And now we will call this function system.out.println, key is at index
In fact, let's return the index, int index is equal to, let's call linear search in which we will pass our array numbers and after that our key
If our index is equal to minus 1, then we will not get the key, in that case we will simply print not found
And in the case of else, we will print our index, key is at index
Here we simply passed our key and array in the linear search function, run a loop in the function
If the number stored on our index is equal to our key, then we will return that index because we got our key there
If we did not get the key on any index, then we will be returning minus 1
So let's run it and check
Our key was at index 4 because we passed the key 10, but let's say we pass the key 20, then what happens in that case?
In that case, it would be printed for us, not found, that is, 20 does not exist anywhere in our entire array
Now you can make a string type array here, which will be named menu
What will we do in the menu? We will keep the same things, first we will write dosa, then we will keep some chole bhature, then we will keep some samosa and so on
So this thing you can replicate with a menu, in fact I will give you this as a homework problem
You have to make an array of your own, in which you have to keep your menu items, in which you have to pass your string key, then you have to check which one is equal to which
Now you can use double equal to for the equality of strings, otherwise there is a function called dot equals in strings, when we take a class about it, we will learn there
For now, you can use equal to equal to to see if it is working or not, you will get some errors here
But I hope that you will try to solve those errors yourself, you will google things
So this is how we adopt linear search, now whenever there is a searching technique, whenever there is a sorting technique, we write a separate program algorithm
So there is a thing called time complexity in it, we will be reading about time complexity later in detail, but for now let's know that time complexity tells us

How much time does a program take to execute, now we will not be able to tell the exact time, but we will be able to tell that when two programs are to be compared, then the program whose time complexity is less is good, and the program whose time complexity is more is slow and bad
Here if we have to see the time complexity for linear search, then where did our major time take, where did it take to search, it took in the loop
How was our loop, for i is equal to 0 to n, here n is the length of the array, and every time we were doing one operation that the value on the ith index should be compared with the key
So in a way we can say that we have done n operations, the length of our array, the same number of times we have checked what is the key here, what is the key here, what is the key here

What will happen in the worst case, in the worst case, our key will not exist and if we have to find 20, then we will check all the indexes one by one, so in this case we will perform n operations, so in a way we can say that our time complexity is big of n

Now this part, who did not understand, there is no need to take tension, later we will be reading it in detail, for those who have a little idea about time complexity, this part was for them that time complexity of linear search is big of n, that is, there are n operations in it.
So our time complexity is proportional to our loop and our loop runs n times.
